paper_title: Searching for vector dark matter with an optomechanical accelerometer
suggested_experiment_name: Optomechanical accelerometer (Si₃N₄ membrane + Be mirror cavity)
coupling_convention: g_BL, dimensionless coupling to B-L charge
notes: This is a PROJECTION paper describing a proposed optomechanical accelerometer detector for vector B-L dark matter. The paper does NOT present measured exclusion limits, but rather theoretical sensitivity projections for a future detector based on a silicon nitride membrane coupled to a beryllium mirror. Key parameters: centimeter-scale membrane (2.5–20 cm), pre-cooled to 10 mK, mechanical Q ≈ 10^9, displacement sensitivity ~2×10^-17 m/√Hz. The projected sensitivity (blue curves in Fig. 2) is claimed to exceed Eöt-Wash bounds by >1 order of magnitude for integration times of minutes over ~0.1% fractional bandwidth near 10 kHz (m_DM ~ 10^-10 eV). Data points extracted from Fig. 2 (B-L coupling, 1-year integration time curves). The paper also discusses B-coupled dark photons (Fig. 4) with similar methodology. Local DM density ρ_DM ≈ 0.4 GeV/cm³ is cited as the standard galactic halo value used in ULDM calculations. Polarization treatment: randomly polarized vector field averaged to ⟨a²⟩ → ⟨a²⟩/3 (Eq. 11, Supplementary I.D). The lower boundary represents the best achievable sensitivity. The coupling type is VectorBL because the paper explicitly discusses coupling to B-L (baryon minus lepton) charge via vector dark photons ('dark photons'). The x-axis is labeled m_DM (eV/c²) and the y-axis is g_BL. Existing constraints from Eöt-Wash, LIGO, and MICROSCOPE experiments are shown for reference.
